content: Metoclopramide is a medication prescribed to alleviate symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, heartburn, stomach pain, bloating, and a persistent sensation of fullness after meals. It may also be used for other medical purposes as determined by your doctor. If you have questions about its uses, consult your healthcare provider or pharmacist. This medication is available in tablet and liquid forms for oral administration. It is essential to follow the instructions on your prescription label precisely. If you have any doubts or need clarification, ask your doctor or pharmacist. Take metoclopramide exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Before starting metoclopramide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you have any allergies to this medication or other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, including amobarbital, insulin, narcotics, phenobarbital, sedatives, tranquilizers, and vitamins. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. Should you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider or dentist that you are taking metoclopramide. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you understand how it affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate the drowsiness caused by metoclopramide, so it is advisable to avoid consuming alcohol while on this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Metoclopramide may cause side effects. Minor side effects include drowsiness, restlessness, fatigue, constipation, and diarrhea. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects include involuntary movements of the limbs or eyes, muscle spasms in the neck, face, or jaw, and mood changes such as depression. If you experience any of these severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Metoclopramide is available under the brand names Metoclopramide Hydrochloride Intensol®, Reglan®, and Reglan® Syrup.
